_meta.description: REAL, CITED ground-truth set of antibacterial drug TARGETS labelled by documented clinical RESISTANCE LIABILITY. HIGH = resistance emerges by a single-step target-site mutation or by loss of a dispensable prodrug-activator. LOW/DURABLE = target-site resistance is rare/slow/multi-step (or undocumented for validated cores). Liability is graded, not truly binary; the binary label is a defensible ordinal collapse for the separation test. Every label traces to a REAL source (CARD, WHO 2023 catalogue, or a landmark peer-reviewed review). No resistance RATE/MIC is used as a model input — only the label (the held-out truth) and the target's zero-data biology are used.

_meta.ordinal_encoding: 0=durable(mechanistic, undrugged core), 1=durable(drugged, resistance rare/slow), 2=multi-step/target-mutation but constrained, 3=single-step target mutation or dispensable-activator loss

targets.mechanism: single-step target-site mutation in the RNA-polymerase Rif-resistance-determining region (RRDR, ~81 bp); >95% of rifampin resistance
single-step target-site mutation in the DNA-gyrase quinolone-resistance-determining region (QRDR, codons 88-94)
topoisomerase-IV QRDR target-site mutation (2nd-step FQ resistance in Gram-negatives)
single-step ribosomal-protein-S12 target-site mutation (K43R/K88R) abolishing aminoglycoside binding
loss/mutation (S315T) of the catalase-peroxidase PRODRUG ACTIVATOR; the activator is dispensable for growth so loss-of-function is tolerated
enoyl-ACP-reductase target: promoter up-regulation and target-site mutation confer INH/ethionamide resistance
arabinosyltransferase target-site mutation (M306V/I) confers ethambutol resistance
loss-of-function of the pyrazinamidase PRODRUG ACTIVATOR (diverse mutations across the gene); the activator is dispensable so LoF is tolerated
dihydropteroate-synthase target-site mutation/insertion (and acquired sul genes) confer sulfonamide resistance

MurA is the fosfomycin target but target-site mutation is a RARE resistance route; clinical resistance is dominated by loss of uptake transporters (glpT/uhpT) and the FosA enzyme -> the TARGET itself is durable
alanine-racemase target of D-cycloserine; clinical resistance is rare and slow to emerge, mechanisms poorly defined
D-Ala-D-Ala ligase target of D-cycloserine; clinical resistance rare/slow
DXR/IspC (MEP pathway) fosmidomycin target; no documented single-step clinical target-site resistance (limited clinical exposure) -> graded-low, honestly flagged as low-exposure

cell-wall biosynthesis core (lipid-II GlcNAc transferase); no documented single-step target-site resistance; highly conserved. UNDRUGGED -> 'resistance rare' partly reflects low clinical exposure (honestly flagged)
cell-wall core (phospho-MurNAc-pentapeptide translocase); durable mechanistic label; UNDRUGGED (low-exposure caveat)
cell-wall core (UDP-N-acetylenolpyruvoylglucosamine reductase); durable mechanistic label; UNDRUGGED (low-exposure caveat)
cell-wall core (UDP-MurNAc-pentapeptide synthetase); durable mechanistic label; UNDRUGGED (low-exposure caveat)
